newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albright proposes NATO to help Albania army.
newsitem.headline: Albright proposes NATO to help Albania army.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright called on Friday for NATO to send an assessment team to Albania to see how the alliance can help the armed forces in the crisis-wracked Balkan country.

"I believe NATO should now send a SHAPE assessment team to Albania in the very near future to determine how the alliance can help restore a functioning, democratically-controlled military to the country," she said in remarks to a new partnership council between NATO and non-alliance states.

SHAPE is NATO's military headquarters in Mons, Belgium. Albright said the results of such a mission should be discussed in the new council -- officially called the Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council (EAPC) -- "so that we can all work together effectively to restore stability to that troubled nation".
Albania spiralled into crisis this year when financial pyramid schemes went bust, bankrupting thousands of Albanians and creating political turmoil.

During a week in which NATO has made new strides in re-fashioning itself, Albright said Albania reflects "the kind of crisis we face in Europe and beyond in the years ahead and of the need for NATO and the EAPC, together with the OSCE (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe) to focus our efforts on preventing conflict".

She applauded the deployment of a multinational troop force to safeguard aid supplies to Albania, saying it "reminds us that from now on, most peace operations in Europe will be conducted by allies and partners working together".
